phase: First held-out run after source-reference and verifier-contract changes; light model only

findings.title: Falsy configuration values and environment variable parsing bugs in Configuration.from_runnable_config
findings.impact: Boolean configuration flags (such as include_source_str: bool = False or ask_for_clarification: bool = False) or any configuration values that evaluate to falsy (e.g., 0, False, empty dict/list, or environment variables containing "0" or "False") are completely discarded by `{k: v for k, v in values.items() if v}`. Furthermore, environment variables returned by `os.environ.get()` are strings, so setting an environment variable to "false" or "0" will be evaluated as truthy in a boolean context or cause type mismatches when passed to fields expecting booleans, ints, or dicts.
findings.preconditions: Calling `Configuration.from_runnable_config` or `MultiAgentConfiguration.from_runnable_config` when boolean flags like `include_source_str` are set to `False` (or omitted, defaulting to `False`), or when numeric/boolean/dict settings are configured with falsy values.
findings.explanation: Line 63 retrieves `os.environ.get(f.name.upper(), configurable.get(f.name))`. `os.environ.get` returns a string or `None`. If an env var is not set, it returns `None`. If set to `"False"` or `"0"`, it is a non-empty string, which is truthy. Line 67 filters out *any* value where `v` is falsy (`if v`), which drops `False`, `0`, `0.0`, empty collections, and leaves missing config values to raise TypeError or fall back incorrectly when `cls(...)` is invoked without defaults (or overriding dataclass defaults with falsy values).

limitations: Finding correctly identifies real source defects, but conflates falsey Python values with nonempty string values in part of its impact text.
Some preconditions mention default False values that do not themselves demonstrate a changed result.
Suggested fix preserves missing/falsy distinction but leaves actual environment type parsing as a comment.
